content.comment_body: Hello! I am aware that [product_name] [version_no] allows up to 400 blocks for use in projects, but I need details about the number of programming lines this device supports. I checked the [document], but only found information regarding blocks.
Since you're mentioning lines, I assume you're programming with LAD. In the [product_name] software, one sheet is the default in the circuit diagram. Please refer to the attached video.

So, does that mean I can create unlimited lines? I've seen other PLCs like [product_name], and they typically specify both the number of Programmable Blocks and Programmable Lines. I've found the block count, but I'm still searching for the maximum number of lines. And yes, I'm using LAD.

No, it's not unlimited. Why not simply determine how many pages can be set? The usable number of lines depends on how many blocks you use per line. For instance, using 2 blocks per line lets you have more lines than using 5 blocks per line. In a parallel connection of 10 inputs, blocks are placed on the top line, meaning 1 line with blocks and 9 lines without. So, calculating the maximum number of lines isn't straightforward.

I understand now. I need this info mainly for marketing reasons. It's common to mention a controller has x blocks and y lines for programming, but explaining this to customers isn't always simple. Maybe I should refer to 'memory available for programming' instead? Regardless, thank you for clarifying.

Exactly, that's why [company_name] doesn't provide precise details (it's difficult to do so). [company_name] gives the maximum block number, but the available memory can only be found in the software. And programming with LAD is considered outdated by some... With FUB, you don't need to worry about lines.
Programming in LAD does result in lots of lines, but in FBD you mainly need space to insert blocks.
In LAD, not the case? That's new to me. Could you explain further? I'd like to learn more from you.

A small program works well in LAD. However, as your program grows in complexity and includes more blocks, it's often better to use FB for programming. FB allows more information per page, making editing and debugging easier. You have full access to all functions in FB, unlike LAD. If you haven't tried FB yet, it's not difficult to learn. There are many tutorials and lessons available on the [company_name] site to help you get started. [url] With some effort, you can learn FB programming in an evening, especially if you're familiar with LAD. Good luck.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for clear limits regarding the maximum number of programming lines in [product_name] [version_no] when using LAD. Although the block count is well-defined, the actual line count depends on programming choices and is not explicitly documented. The conversation also touched on differences between LAD and FB/FBD programming, with users noting the lack of straightforward information and expressing some frustration over the ambiguity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clearer documentation or software guidance specifying the maximum number of programming lines, not just blocks, so they can easily communicate these limits to customers.
